correctness.rationale: A neighborhood over the named base is admissible exactly when it is triangle-free: otherwise adding the point creates a K4, and otherwise each finite one-point extension embeds over the base. Homogeneity makes this a single complete type per pattern, and arbitrarily many pairwise nonadjacent copies of the new vertex witness nonalgebraicity. For a tree line graph, every triangle is a triple of edges at a single vertex; subcubicity makes the forbidden sets exactly the complete three-edge stars. In inclusion–exclusion the union of stars at W has 3|W|-e_H(W) edges, because precisely internal branch edges are counted twice. The union of three or more stars contains at least seven edges since H is a forest. Thus degree 3 extracts the star count and degree 5 isolates adjacent pairs after subtracting the single-star contributions. Across orders the linear coefficient recovers m. Within each order at most five, the only applicable shapes are a path and, at orders four and five, the unique three-arm spider. At order six the degree-sum identity bounds the number of branch vertices by two: the path, the two positive arm partitions of five into three parts, and the adjacent two-branch tree exhaust the cases. The spiders both give (1+z)^5-z³(1+z)^2=1+5z+10z²+9z³+3z⁴, uniquely colliding; their line graphs have different degree multisets. This is a collision on six vertices of T, hence on five named vertices of L(T). For each n≥6 the two stated arm partitions are unequal and have the same total, and their line graphs retain the arm lengths along the paths attached to the unique triangle. An independent leaf-extension enumeration with rooted canonical codes and degree-conditioned tree dynamic programming agrees coefficientwise with the star formula for all subcubic trees through order 12, yielding class counts (1,1,2,2,4) and polynomial counts (1,1,2,2,3) at orders 2–6.
residual_risks: Finite replay is corroboration of the formula and an exact small-order check, not proof of the all-order identity. The result is an adjacency-count grading over named parameters, not an invariant of higher-arity type spaces.

value.rationale: This natural graded type invariant retains the number of branch points and their internal edge count but cannot even recover arm lengths. Giving both directions of useful information, an exact smallest failure rather than merely a witness, and simple infinite families of connected witnesses makes the result useful for reconstruction with a logical count. The value is the identified information loss and sharp boundary, not the standard counting method or another small table by itself.
residual_risks: The dependence theorem is not a classification of all equal spectra; neither full branch-forest reconstruction nor a result for general K4-free bases is claimed.
